records.name: England
records.current_summary: Worse than the pre-2025 position, and worse than Wales on official posture. The EHRC's updated Code of Practice for Services, Public Functions and Associations was laid 21 May 2026 and came into force on 5 August 2026 as statutory guidance (replacing the 2011 code): single-sex spaces open to the public — toilets, gym changing rooms, hospital wards, rape-crisis centres — should be organised by biological sex, with trans people directed to gender-neutral or birth-sex facilities. The guidance binds service providers UK-wide but is administered in England, and it is the map's clearest 'you may be refused' signal. Its legal predicate is For Women Scotland v The Scottish Ministers (UK Supreme Court, 16 April 2025): 'sex' and 'woman' in the Equality Act 2010 mean biological/registered sex, and a Gender Recognition Certificate does not change legal sex for Equality Act purposes. The ruling has immediate visitor-facing consequences in England's transport and custody settings: following it, British Transport Police moved (17 April 2025, stated interim position) to strip-searching trans women detained on the rail network by male officers, reversing the acquired-gender policy for GRC holders. Anti-trans offending is statistically invisible in the official record: England and Wales reported 115,990 hate crimes in the year to March 2025 across five monitored strands, and transgender identity is not a separately recorded strand (unlike Scotland and Northern Ireland). The strongest practical gradient inside the unit is London — visible community, dedicated services, dedicated hate-crime policing — versus the rest of England; no sourced sub-England region-level evidence was found, so the unit is assessed whole.

sources.claim: BBC News (19 June 2026): a judge (Lady Ross, Court of Session) ruled Scottish Prison Service guidance allowing some trans prisoners to be housed by gender identity unlawful — sex segregation in prisons must be based on biological sex, applying the UK Supreme Court's April 2025 'definition of a woman' ruling. The judgment confirms the biological-sex custody logic that the same UK-wide ruling imposes on England's prison and custody decisions; the first minister said the government will consider the judgment (the Supreme Court had already held Article 8 confers no automatic right to opposite-biological-sex accommodation).

BBC News (5 February 2026): argument of the same judicial review, in which government lawyers said a blanket rule housing trans prisoners by sex at birth would breach human rights and create an unacceptable suicide risk, while For Women Scotland called the identity-based policy 'Orwellian'; the case tests how far the UK Supreme Court's April 2025 ruling (cited as the predicate for England's EHRC code and BTP strip-search policy) reaches into prison accommodation UK-wide.

records.name: Queensland
records.current_summary: Queensland is a protective outlier on the legal side: first in Australia to criminally prohibit conversion practices — Public Health Act 2005 ch 5B (s.213F), in force 20 August 2020, covering practices aimed at changing or suppressing sexual orientation or gender identity, with named prohibited techniques — and it drafted a complete anti-discrimination rewrite (Anti-Discrimination Bill 2024) with a modernised 'gender identity' attribute aligned to the Yogyakarta Principles, separated from sex-characteristics provisions, plus vilification offences; the rewrite was still in consultation in the documents reviewed. The one operationally adverse fact for a detained visitor is custody placement: Queensland sits outside the four self-identification jurisdictions (NSW, Victoria, ACT, Tasmania), so prison placement turns on surgical-intervention status or case-by-case assessment — meaning 'some trans women can be placed in men's prisons' here, unlike in the self-ID states.

records.name: Roraima
records.current_summary: No state facility, expression or ordinance law was documented for Roraima: the national protective-but-porous framework applies unchanged. On record it sits at the safe extreme of the Brazilian map — no killings of trans people were found recorded in the state for 2024, and in 2025 it falls in the lowest national band (0-3 cases) — though the dossier stresses these are floors from systematic under-counting and a single case would swing the rate in so small a state. Federally administered indigenous territories with parallel community authority lie within Roraima; no trans-specific evidence was found for them.

sources.claim: Wikipedia overview of LGBTQ rights in Brazil: STF rulings give gender identity/expression protection without surgery or court order, the 2019 equating of LGBTphobia with racism, and non-binary birth-certificate recognition handled case-by-case per federative unit — Roraima's row notes a 2025 free judicial action permitting trans and non-binary rectifications, with no state statute establishing the option. Useful as the national legal backdrop; no state criminalisation.

Outright International Brazil country overview (updated 12 March 2026): marriage equality since 2013 under repeal pressure, 2019 STF hate-crime equivalence, self-determination gender markers, world's highest absolute trans-murder toll with interior vs capital geography, conservative-Congress anti-LGBTIQ surge against a pro-rights executive — the national frame applied uniformly in Roraima.

Law-firm expat guide (updated 5 April 2026) to LGBTQ+ legal rights in Brazil: no comprehensive federal anti-discrimination statute but progressive STF jurisprudence (marriage, adoption, marker changes without surgery, phobia-as-racism); explicitly warns the framework is 'progressive on paper and uneven in practice', with protections concentrated in major cities — the interior-unevenness caveat that covers Roraima.

records.name: Acre
records.current_summary: Brazil's uniform national framework applies with no state-specific law or enforcement pattern documented. In ANTRA's annual state-by-state killings dossier, no killings were found recorded in Acre for 2024. Acre is among the least populous federation units, so a single case moves its rate enormously - the recorded zero carries little evidential weight. No deviation material enough to treat apart from the national position was found.

sources.claim: Wikipedia overview of LGBTQ rights in Brazil: the national legal timeline - recognition of same-sex unions and marriage (STF 2011/CNJ 2013), adoption, discrimination protections, gender identity and expression (the March 2018 rulings allowing name/gender-marker change without surgery), conversion therapy, military service and blood donation, plus a section listing non-binary marker rules by federative unit. Framework is national; state-level variation is not covered by this page.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2012 -> March 2026 file): same-sex relations legal throughout the country; legal gender recognition possible by self-determination; a 2019 Supreme Court ruling prohibits discrimination and hate crimes on SOGI grounds; marriage equality since 2013 with active repeal efforts in Congress; Brazil continues to have one of the highest rates of violence against sexual and gender minorities, particularly trans people; 3,000+ openly LGBTQ candidates ran in the 2024 municipal elections; a 2025 Superior Court of Justice ruling allows nonbinary civil-registry amendments; executive pro-rights vs a conservative legislature generating a surge of anti-LGBTIQ proposals.

Brazilian law-firm guide to LGBTQ+ legal rights for expats (updated April 2026): protections were established by the judiciary (STF/CNJ) rather than statute - same-sex marriage, spousal-visa equality, joint adoption, name and gender-marker change without surgery, and criminalisation of homophobia/transphobia as equivalent to racism; major cities broadly welcoming with legal infrastructure accustomed to same-sex marriages and name changes; the guide states smaller cities and rural areas may present more social friction, 'though the legal rights are identical nationwide'.
